blocks.text: The following article provides information on how to configure step-up authentication in the Zscaler Admin Console to allow dynamic requests for stronger authentication when users attempt to access sensitive resources or when risk signals indicate a potential threat.
Before configuring step-up authentication, ensure that:

blocks.item: Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 or later is deployed for the users in your organization.
Authentication Service is enabled for both admins and users.
Step-up authentication is enabled for Authentication Service, Internet & SaaS (ZIA), and Private Access (ZPA) tenants.

blocks.text: To learn more about prerequisites specific to an external identity provider (IdP), refer to the external IdP's product documentation.
Step-up authentication is supported only with OIDC-based external IdP integrations. Any IdP that supports OIDC-based authentication with ACR values can be configured for step-up authentication.

blocks.item: 1. Configure authentication levels.
2. Enable ACR values and configure the necessary policies in the external IdPs.

In the external IdP integrated with Authentication Service, configure the necessary ACR values and authentication policies. The configuration of ACR values and the necessary policies depend on the specific external IdP. To learn more about the configuration, refer to the respective product documentation.

The following list provides detailed steps for configuring ACR values and authentication policies in select IdPs. However, Authentication Service supports step-up authentication for OIDC-based external IdP integrations beyond what is listed here:
Enabling Step-Up Authentication in Entra ID
Enabling Step-Up Authentication in PingOne
3. Map authentication levels and ACR values.
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Authentication > External Identities.
Locate the IdP under the Primary Identity Provider (or Secondary Identity Providers) tab and click the Edit icon.
On the Edit External Identity page:
Select the Advanced Configurations tab.

Under the Levels to Authentication Context Mapping section, enter the ACR claim value for each authentication level. To learn more about the supported ACR claims in external IdP, refer to the respective product documentation.
Ensure that you map proper ACR claims for each level depending on the hierarchy. The highest level of authentication must be mapped to the ACR claim value for the strongest context.
See image.
Click Save.
4. Configure access policies in supported Zscaler services.
You can configure the necessary policies in the following Zscaler services as required:

Private Access: Configure Access Policies for the target application or app segment with the Conditional Access as the Rule Action. Ensure that the necessary authentication level is selected using the Step-up Authentication Level field.

Internet & SaaS: Configure the URL Filtering Policy and Cloud App Control Policies with the Conditional Access as the Action. Ensure that the necessary authentication level is selected using the Authentication Level field.
